newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea steps in again, sells dlrs - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea steps in again, sells dlrs - dealers.

text.p: The Bank of Korea sold dollars at around 891.20 won in Monday afternoon trading in its second intervention in less than two hours to slow the won's fall, dealers said.
The won was trading at around 891.50 won shortly before the central bank stepped in, they said.
Earlier on Monday, the central bank sold dollars at around 892 won, dealers said.
"The won was slipping back when the central bank intervened again," a foreign bank dealer said.
Bank of Korea officials were not available for comment.
Dealers said the intervention was seen aimed at supporting the won in the aftermath of recent plunges of local currencies vis-a-vis the U.S. unit in Thailand and the Philippines.
